discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard LambdaCDM cosmological model
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe transformed cosmology from an order-of-magnitude science into a precision discipline. Through a carefully designed differential instrument and exceptional control of systematics, Bennett (PI), Page (instrument lead) and Spergel (lead of analysis and interpretation) produced full-sky maps of CMB temperature and polarisation anisotropies. These fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent-level accuracy, confirmed spatial flatness, measured the baryon and dark-matter densities, found the early reionisation of the universe, and detected the small departure from scale invariance of the primordial fluctuations that inflation predicts. Independently of supernovae, WMAP showed that dark energy makes up about 70% of the cosmic budget, and it gave the concordance LambdaCDM framework that all later surveys test. The 2006 prize honoured COBE's discovery of the anisotropies. WMAP turned them into the fundamental measurement of our cosmological model.
